slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: Remember a Failed Breakdown requires price to lose and recover a significant low.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: A significant low has three possible definitions. 1) The prior days low 2) A multi-hour low/ a low that goes 20+ points or 3) A cluster or shelf of lows.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: At 7421 we had number 1: The prior days low and 7421 was the low of day Friday.

slides.sentence: This is an obvious entry if triggered.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: As always with Failed Breakdowns though the golden rule is if you just rush in long on the recovery of the significant low, you lose.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: Prior to entry you HAVE TO see either: 1) One of the two acceptance types.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: Acceptance is price action that we must see prior to entry, in order to prevent us from rushing in and getting trapped.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: It generally involves price trying to sell at or above the significant low then returning to it.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: By doing so, price is telling us that it wants to be there so that when we long the recovery of the significant low, we won’t rush in long, get trapped, and have price selloff. 2) The Non-Acceptance protocol.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: The non-acceptance protocol only triggers when price recovers the significant low (7421) by 5 points and holds above for a couple minutes.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: This typically triggers in high volatility, fast markets where price does not pause around the significant low (7421) and just rips through.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: Remember 5 points above the significant low is the danger zone for Failed Breakdowns and where most losses occur.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: If entering in this zone you need clear acceptance and if you don’t see it or it is too noisy or uncertain, just wait for the non-acceptance protocol.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: Remember the non-acceptance protocol automatically activates when price recovers the significant low (7421) by 5 points (7426) and holds at or above 7426 for a few minutes.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: The non-acceptance protocol typically triggers for shallow (under 10 point flush of the significant low) and fast Failed Breakdowns, but you can use it for any Failed Breakdown.

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown

slides.section: Sunday Evening and the 7398 Failed Breakdown
slides.sentence: We ripped to 7450+ this morning after, then dipped to 7374.
It is worth noting after 3pm we then got another quality Failed Breakdown.
I wrote yesterday at 4pm: “There is not much below there until 7377.
This is a decent support and if its a controlled grind lower into the zone, one can bid it.
If its a total free fall though, it is essential to never knife catch.

Instead, wait for it to defend and recover 7384 to get long and this is a quality entry.”
By 2:50PM, ES sold down to 7374.
In doing so, ES lost a big shelf of lows that formed overnight/this morning at 7377.
There is a very clear shelf of lows here with multiple touches between Sunday at 930PM and Monday at 2:30AM.
We swept that shelf at 2:50PM as stated down to 7374, and recovered.
One could have taken the long here via the non-acceptance protocol since this was very fast. 7377+5s83.
Long above 7383.
Since this was very fast, I was not able to get in until 7402.
I managed this level though: Locked in 75% profits at 7414 1st up, left 25% to run.
Locked in more at 7421 2nd up, left 10% to go.

I do this trade recap section for one reason mostly - to give new traders a sense of what running a system looks like in reality because if new traders today are anything like I was starting off, they have a laughably wrong idea of what profitable trading looks like (and as a result, aren’t profitable).
It’s not about trading 15 times a day, flipping back and forth long and short, catching every move the market makes.
Trading takes me about 15 minutes per day and I catch whatever piece happens to correlate with my edge.
Sometimes its 1% of the action, sometimes its 100%, some days its 0.
I don’t trade because I am bored, have FOMO, am greedy, have an opinion on what price may do, read what an influencer said will happen.
I could be 100% sure price is going to do something, and I still won’t trade.
I trade because price came into a zone dictated by my plan, and produced my edge in that zone (Failed Breakdown).
I don’t care what price does outside that context.
All other action is irrelevant.
It doesnt matter if price sells 200 points.
Nothing to do with me or my edge.
It took me years as a beginner - unfortunately - to realize this is what profitable trading looks like because there is a whole industry of people selling a fabricated version of what it looks like.
This version involves people flipping back and forth long and short everyday, catching every move.

It wasn’t until I had the opportunity to speak to a mentor of mine a few years into my career (and after a few years of learning) that while I was trading to catch every move and get rich in a day, this particular mentor was ecstatic if he got 5, 10, 15 points a session.
Many weeks he would go 2-3 days with no trades if a fat pitch didn’t appear only take a 6 point trade.
I do the same template daily: I do 1-2 trades daily.
These trades are typically before 11am, or after 3pm.
I often enter between 730am and 830am, but this is not a hard rule.
If there is no good entry in that morning window, I will enter later.
I enter only at pre-planned, high conviction zones, on A+ setups.
I rarely trade the window between 11am and 2pm as its often chop.
First trade is a win in the morning, I hold the runner and I stop trading, only rarely trying one more in the afternoon.
First trade is a loss, I trade one more.
Both trades are losses, I quit for the day.

basic_themes:
Heading into today, I verified my positioning at the close yesterday at 4pm: “ I am still holding my 10% long runner from last Thursday’s 6pm 7345 Failed Breakdown, provided in Thursday’s 4pm newsletter. My most recent entry was the 7402 Level Reclaim at 9:55AM.”
There were a few things to note heading into today:
1) Readers know that I talk everyday about the two siblings in ES. These siblings are elevator down sell and short squeeze, they are always paired together, and this is the tendency we exploit to generate our entries. Elevator down sell refers to a sharp flush where ES cuts through many supports with ease. This is usually how ES sells off. It rallies slowly (stairs up) and sells in a straight line (elevator down). This typically lasts a few minutes to a few hours. Rarely, a whole day. We typically see one elevator down move per day, with the only exception being on Mode 1 green days (these are open to close trend days to the upside). Mode 1 days (open to close trend days) are only 10% of sessions overall. After Elevator Down sells, ES puts in a face ripping short squeeze. The catch though is the squeeze only occurs when ES puts in a Failed Breakdown (big low flushes, traps, recovers) or Level Reclaim. Not a moment before, and if you try knife before this trigger event, you will lose.
We got this dynamic Wednesday morning. Wednesday morning ES sold 60 points into around 10:50AM to 7399. Shortly after ES put in a nice Failed Breakdown of a big low at 7410 from 8pm Tuesday evening. We ripped afterwards for the short squeeze to 7530+ highs Thursday.
From there? Elevator down to 7421 by 9:50AM Friday morning. Shortly after - at 10am - ES put in a Failed Breakdown. Specifically, from 430am to 930AM ES set a nice shelf of lows at 7435 from which we rallied 35 points. That 7435 shelf swept to 7421, recovered, and we ripped to 7460+ Friday.
Then Sunday evening? Same drill. We went elevator down to 7375. In doing so lost a big low at 7398 (the daily low from last Wednesday). We recovered it around 4:15AM this morning, and we ripped vertically to 7450’s.
Elevator down, Failed Breakdown, Short Squeeze. The cycle repeats over and over.
You get the drill. For every action in ES there is an equal and opposite reaction. Whenever you see a big red bar, whether it lasts a few minutes, a few hours - or once or twice a month - a full day, you can expect the squeeze to be of equal ferocity. Bears never get anything for free in ES on an intraday basis - they have not in over 100 years of S&P 500 trading and never will. The larger the sell, the larger the squeeze(you can think of every point of red as going into a machine that will later spit out 0.5 to 10 points of green), but the squeeze only commences on a Failed Breakdown.
Elevator Down, Failed Breakdown, Short Squeeze. Elevator Down, Failed Breakdown, Short Squeeze. It applies in uptrends and downtrends. The only difference between up and downtrend is in downtrends the squeezes will not retrace 100% of the sell and will make a lower high.
2) The basic theme heading into today was that ES was rangebound. I expanded on this Friday at 4pm and spoke about what to do with it:
Bull case Monday: ES finds itself stuck inside a new range now which is mostly 7472 resistance, and support at 7421. 7435 and 7458 are key levels inside this range. The task for bulls Monday is to defend this range (or quick trap below) then break it out. This may look something like defend 7435 (or quick trap below 7421) then rip up the range to 7458, 7472. Perhaps final dip there, then breakout targts 7496, 7508, 7520. Above there, we head back to all time highs. We are in an awkward spot now in the middle of the range so there are limited low risk spots to add on strength. Perhaps 7458 reclaims is one higher complexity entry.
3) Finally, while I discuss plenty of structures and levels above, its vital that we do not use any of the above to make predictions. Our job as traders is never to predict what price will do (literally impossible on an intraday basis). Our job is to plan zones, wait for price to present our setups at those zones, then manage the trade systematically level to level. I am not exagerating at all when I say the core difference between winning and losing traders is that losing traders are obssessed with knowing where price will go. Professionals don’t care - they let price pick the path and react. This allows one to trade what they see, not what they think, and not be affected by bias. When you predict, you are giving yourself a bias which blinds you from objectively trading the action. Price traps by its nature and takes the pathway engineered to cause the maximum pain to retail traders. You can pretend that it is a supercomputer that is intentionally trying to ensure that no retail traders profit from any large move, and ensure they are all stopped out, trapped, and frustrated before one occurs.
It is for this reason that instead of predicting the path and getting trapped non-stop, we need to flip the script and trade the traps: Wait on the Failed Breakdowns, manage profits level to level (thereby never predicting how far any move will go) and let runners work. Rinse and repeat daily. The second you start imagining price paths or trading on them, you’ve already lost the game.
Here is the difference in the types of statements professional traders make vs retail traders in this regard. A retail trader will make proclamations. They will say “We are going to sell 80 points, then rally 20, then sell another 100”. Or they say “We lost X leve, the top is in, we are heading lower”. Professionals say “If price tests X level, flushes it, and recovers, I long for a lvl to lvl move”. “If price rallies to Z level, I short for a level to level move”, “If price does none of the above, I do nothing”. Be a trader, not a fortune teller and don’t expect price to do anything. When I sit down to trade, I wipe my mind clean of any expectations, predictions, or opinions on direction. Have a plan for exactly where and how you want to engage, let price choose the path, then you can react accordingly. If your doing this right, you should be able to enter a session “feeling” the most bearish you have felt in a year, but if a Failed Breakdown triggers off the open, you are long. From there, all trades are managed systematically level to level, again never predicting how far any move will go.
With this in mind, let’s look at how yesterday’s execution plan applied to today’s action.
